name: L. D. Pettit
role: Bone buyer and stage owner based at Belfield
bio: L. D. Pettit of Deadwood made Belfield his headquarters in 1884, holding heavy contracts for bones and paying pickers $8 a ton in cash. His family arrived from Crook City in one of his stages in August 1884, and that September he was building a residence there.

moments.label: Paying $8 a ton for bones at Belfield

mentions: …the men implicated will be made an example of.  Quite a trade has sprung up in the bone business here. L. D. Pettit, of Deadwood, the prince of rustlers, who holds heavy contracts for bones, makes Belfield his headquarters, and what is better, pays over to ye hard-working bone pickers…
Mr. Pettit's family has arrived from Crook City in one of Pettit's finest stages, which is the most metropolitan thing that ever honored the town of Belfield.

L. D. Pettit, of Belfield, stopped at Medora a short time this week en reute to Billings and other points in connection with his fast increasing bone business.
